front: Entropy of a uniform distribution over $M$ states
back: $\log M$, the maximum. A point mass has entropy 0.
Probabilities $\frac12,\frac14,\frac18,\frac1{16},4\times\frac1{64}$: entropy 2 bits; code lengths $1,2,3,4,6,6,6,6$ give average 2 bits versus 3 for a flat code.
$H(p,q)=-\sum_xp(x)\log q(x)$: average code length when the truth is $p$ and the code is built for $q$.

No. $\mathrm{KL}(p\|q)\ne\mathrm{KL}(q\|p)$ in general (e.g. $0.531$ vs $0.737$ bits for $(0.9,0.1)$ vs $(0.5,0.5)$).

front: Cross-entropy loss with a one-hot label
back: $-\ln q_c$, the negative log-probability of the true class. Over a dataset: the negative log-likelihood.
$\mathrm{KL}(p\|q_\theta)=\text{const}-\mathbb E_p[\ln q_\theta]\approx\text{const}+\mathrm{NLL}/N$, so both have the same minimiser.
